title: NIST SP 800-82: Section 5: OT/IoT Threat and Vulnerability Overview
content: NIST SP 800-82 Rev 3: Guide to Operational Technology (OT) & IoT Security - Section 5: OT/IoT Threat and Vulnerability Overview: Operational Technology and IoT devices are vulnerable to volumetric network denial-of-service (DDoS/DoS) attacks, unauthorized command injection, ARP spoofing, and rogue gateway masquerading. Constrained IoT microcontrollers lack cryptographic hardware acceleration, making them prone to resource exhaustion when bombarded with high-rate packet floods.
keywords: NIST SP 800-82 OT IoT network segmentation Purdue model Rate anomaly containment Section 5: OT/IoT Threat and Vulnerability Overview

title: NIST SP 800-82: Section 6.2: Network Segmentation & Purdue Architecture
content: NIST SP 800-82 Rev 3: Guide to Operational Technology (OT) & IoT Security - Section 6.2: Network Segmentation & Purdue Architecture: IoT field devices, sensors, and actuators must be segregated into dedicated security zones (Purdue Level 1/0) using firewalls, VLANs, and micro-segmentation. Cross-zone communication must be strictly restricted to stateful inspection proxies to isolate lateral movement.
keywords: NIST SP 800-82 OT IoT network segmentation Purdue model Rate anomaly containment Section 6.2: Network Segmentation & Purdue Architecture

title: NIST SP 800-82: Section 6.4: Incident Containment & Human-in-the-Loop Mandates
content: NIST SP 800-82 Rev 3: Guide to Operational Technology (OT) & IoT Security - Section 6.4: Incident Containment & Human-in-the-Loop Mandates: Defensive automated response mechanisms on safety-critical IoT (e.g., medical infusion devices, industrial programmable logic controllers) must prioritize non-destructive isolation (quarantine VLAN) over abrupt port shutdown. Automated mitigations must provide transparent explainability and enforce human-in-the-loop analyst authorization before persistent configuration changes.
keywords: NIST SP 800-82 OT IoT network segmentation Purdue model Rate anomaly containment Section 6.4: Incident Containment & Human-in-the-Loop Mandates

title: NIST SP 800-82: Section 6.7: Detection Signatures & Flow Rate Anomaly Monitoring
content: NIST SP 800-82 Rev 3: Guide to Operational Technology (OT) & IoT Security - Section 6.7: Detection Signatures & Flow Rate Anomaly Monitoring: Network flow anomalies such as rapid deviations in packet rate (Rate > 1000 pkts/s), source burst rate (Srate), destination drift (Drate), and irregular TCP flags (excessive SYN without ACK or unexpected RST/FIN counts) are primary indicators of ongoing denial of service or network reconnaissance.

title: NIST SP 800-53: Control SC-5 (Denial-of-Service Protection)
content: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Control SC-5: Denial-of-Service Protection. Guidance: Implement boundary protection, ingress rate-limiting, SYN cookies, and adaptive traffic throttling at the IoT network gateway to restrict volumetric flood attacks and maintain availability of critical services.
keywords: NIST SP 800-53 SC-5 Denial-of-Service Protection SYN cookies ARP inspection boundary protection

title: NIST SP 800-53: Control SC-7 (Boundary Protection & Dynamic ARP Inspection)
content: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Control SC-7: Boundary Protection & Dynamic ARP Inspection. Guidance: Enforce managed network interfaces, DHCP snooping, Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI), and 802.1X port security to prevent adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) ARP spoofing and IP header forgery.
keywords: NIST SP 800-53 SC-7 Boundary Protection & Dynamic ARP Inspection SYN cookies ARP inspection boundary protection

title: NIST SP 800-53: Control SI-4 (Information System Monitoring & Anomaly Detection)
content: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Control SI-4: Information System Monitoring & Anomaly Detection. Guidance: Continuously monitor inbound and outbound network telemetry for anomalous protocol usage, abnormal inter-arrival time (IAT), header length fluctuations, and unexpected connection state flags.
keywords: NIST SP 800-53 SI-4 Information System Monitoring & Anomaly Detection SYN cookies ARP inspection boundary protection

title: NIST SP 800-53: Control IR-4 (Incident Handling & Response Procedures)
content: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 Control IR-4: Incident Handling & Response Procedures. Guidance: Formulate prioritized playbooks for volumetric DDoS, single-endpoint DoS, and spoofing intrusions with step-by-step forensic logging, containment isolation, and post-incident verification.
keywords: NIST SP 800-53 IR-4 Incident Handling & Response Procedures SYN cookies ARP inspection boundary protection

title: NIST IR 8259A: Device Identification & Hardware Identity
content: NIST IR 8259A Core Baseline: Device Identification & Hardware Identity. Details: Each IoT device must possess a unique, verifiable identity (e.g. IEEE 802.1AR DevID, immutable MAC address) to prevent spoofing, MAC cloning, and rogue device impersonation.
keywords: NIST IR 8259A IoT device identity MAC cloning botnet prevention Device Identification & Hardware Identity

title: NIST IR 8259A: Device Configuration & Secure Defaults
content: NIST IR 8259A Core Baseline: Device Configuration & Secure Defaults. Details: Disable legacy protocols (Telnet, unencrypted HTTP, cleartext SNMP) to eliminate trivial attack vectors and prevent IoT nodes from being recruited into Mirai-like botnet swarms.
keywords: NIST IR 8259A IoT device identity MAC cloning botnet prevention Device Configuration & Secure Defaults

title: NIST IR 8259A: Data Protection & Network Interface Restraint
content: NIST IR 8259A Core Baseline: Data Protection & Network Interface Restraint. Details: Restrict open listening sockets to authorized management ports and isolate IoT data transport to encrypted channels (TLS 1.3, DTLS, MQTT over TLS).
keywords: NIST IR 8259A IoT device identity MAC cloning botnet prevention Data Protection & Network Interface Restraint
